draft.title: Representation in non-fiction and media
card: A non-fiction or media text does not show an event exactly as it was. It represents it, which means it presents a version of people and events.
the writer or producer chooses which facts, voices, images and details to include and which to leave out.
the angle and wording used to present what is included, such as the headline, the camera shot, the order of information or the label given to a person.
Selection and framing can reflect the text's context (who made it, when and for whom) and its purpose, such as to inform, persuade or entertain.
draft.remember: Every media text is a version of events, shaped by what it picks and how it presents it.

a.q: A news report on a council vote quotes only residents who oppose a new road. What does this show about the report?
opts: It selected some voices and left out others
It framed the road using a misleading headline
It reflects a purpose of entertaining the audience
It gave an exact record of the whole community
a.why: Choosing whose words to include is selection, and here it leaves out other views. The report is not an exact record of the community, because it shows only one side. We are told nothing about the headline, so framing through a headline cannot be assumed.
a.clue: Think about whose words were chosen and whose were left out.

b.q: Two reports cover the same school fun run. One is headed 'Hundreds of students cheer on runners'. The other is headed 'Fun run closes main street for hours'. What best explains the difference?
opts: Each frames the event to suit its own angle and audience
One report is fiction and the other is non-fiction
One report has invented facts about the fun run
Only one report is allowed to choose its details
b.why: Both headlines can be true, but each frames the same event differently. One stresses community spirit, the other stresses disruption, which suits different audiences. Having different angles does not mean either report is made up.
b.clue: Both headlines could be true at the same time.

a.best: It selected some voices and left out others

b.best: Each frames the event to suit its own angle and audience
